title: Q4 Roadmap Launch Readiness - Engineering Prep
summary: Internal engineering and product sync to confirm launch readiness for the Q4 runtime improvements. Reviewed recent incident (memory leak), validated performance SLOs, confirmed rollout gating criteria, and assigned action items for final load testing and post-deploy monitoring. Decided to delay one low-risk feature to post-launch.
topics: Incident review: memory leak in continuous batching
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-30 08:30 - 09:45 PT | Duration: 75 minutes
Attendees: Asha, Marcus, Riley, Priya, Diego, Nina

00:00 Asha: okay, good morning everyone, thanks for joining the Q4 launch readiness engineering prep, we have 75 minutes, main goals are incident review, perf SLO check, and finalize rollout gates
00:22 Marcus: quick note, I pushed the new batching change to the staging cluster last night, saw about a 12% improvement in p95 but a small mem increase at high concurrency, might be related to the K-V cache retention policy
00:42 Priya: yeah, I saw that, the memory trend spikes around 20k concurrent requests in the test harness, we should run it again with the new GC flag, I suspect the leak is in the k v cache eviction path, possibly a pointer hold from the tensor pool, sorry fuzzy there, noisy logs tho
01:10 Riley: can we summarize the incident timeline, Diego do you have the postmortem draft?
01:18 Diego: I put a draft in the drive, short version: 2026-11-28 high traffic test replicated a memory leak after continuous batching change, caused two pod restarts, auto-recovery OK but latency SLOs breached for ~7 minutes, root cause suspected as delayed KV cache eviction after large sequences
01:45 Asha: key question - is the fix ready and validated? What's the confidence level?
01:52 Marcus: fix is in review, we added explicit cache release in the runtime code path, unit tests pass, integration on staging shows no leak in 6h run but we need a longer soak with realistic sequences, low risk but want a green light from SRE
02:18 Priya: I'll run a 48 hour soak starting today, with traffic shape matching production peak, and include the GC flag trial, I expect preliminary results in 24 hours but final by Thursday, that gives us an extra buffer
02:40 Nina: product question - does the leak affect dedicated customers differently than hosted? Any data residency or private deploy concerns?
02:52 Marcus: impact is system-level, dedicated customers running with large sequence workloads could hit the spike earlier; private deployments with older runtimes won't see it unless they upgrade, so we need to call that out in release notes and recommend the patch
03:20 Riley: we should also consider canary size and monitoring thresholds - set a canary at 10% traffic for 2 hours, then 50% for 4 hours if no regressions
03:36 Asha: agreed, also add an automated rollback threshold when error rate >1% or p95 > 500ms for more than 5 minutes
03:50 Priya: action: I'll add those monit thresholds to the runbook and configure alerts.
03:58 Diego: QA will run the regression suite once Marcus merges the fix; I have a few heavyweight prompt sets that reproduce the leak behavior locally, will run them at scale
04:15 Marcus: quick aside — the quantization patch interacts unexpectedly with continuous batching, in some paths it double-counts buffer offsets, might be separate but worth watching
04:34 Asha: do we need to pull that quantization change from the launch?
04:40 Marcus: it's safe to decouple; we can ship the batching fix first, leave quantization in the backlog for a follow-up release unless we find a showstopper
04:55 Nina: product reprioritized feature flags then? We were planning to enable compressed kv cache in the launch, sounds like we delay that?
05:05 Riley: yes, defer compressed KV cache to post-launch to keep the blast radius small
05:18 Asha: okay lets capture decisions: defer compressed KV cache; ship batching fix; run 48h soak; set canary and rollback thresholds; QA regression and load test results before full rollout
05:34 Marcus: perf SLOs check — current target p95 < 300ms for hosted small seq workloads, p95 < 450ms for larger seqs on dedicated - are we comfortable with those numbers?
05:50 Priya: with the batching improvement we're at p95 ~280ms on staging for small seqs, but under heavy concurrency it pushes to ~410ms without the GC flag, so that ties back to the leak issue
06:10 Asha: any blockers for meeting the SLOs by launch?
06:18 Marcus: main blocker is validation under realistic concurrency, also need to tune kernel selection heuristics for longer sequences — I have a PR that improves selection but need more perf data
06:36 Diego: qa note, integration tests show flakiness in function/tool-calling sequences, sometimes the structured output parse fails under heavy load, filing a bug for that
06:52 Nina: product ask — do we have a comms plan for customers if we delay the compressed KV cache feature? Should marketing and support be looped in
07:05 Asha: yes, Nina and Diego will draft release notes and a support FAQ, include recommended upgrade path and mitigations for private deployments
07:18 Priya: SRE checklist recap: run 48h soak, add canary alerts, configure auto-rollback, smoke test the upgraded runtime on a small dedicated cluster, share Prometheus dashboards and runbook links
07:36 Riley: operationally, gating criteria to move from canary to full rollout: green metrics for 24 hours at 50% traffic, error budget intact, no memory regressions in Prometheus histograms
07:55 Marcus: timeline — if soak passes and QA signoff, we can start canary on Dec 3rd; full rollout potentially Dec 6th, but fuzz schedule by 48h if we see issues
08:14 Asha: ok, next steps and owners please
08:20 Priya: I'll run soak and post results to the thread, due 2026-12-02 08:00 PT
08:28 Diego: QA regression and heavy-prompt results, due 2026-12-02 17:00 PT
08:34 Marcus: merge patch after review, coordinate with Priya, target merge 2026-12-01 end of day
08:40 Nina: draft release notes and support FAQ, due 2026-12-03
08:46 Riley: prepare rollback runbook and canary playbook, due 2026-12-02
08:55 Asha: decision to cut compressed KV cache, put in backlog, we'll announce in the public notes; also confirm that SOC 2 / sock two docs not impacted by this change
09:12 Priya: quick security note — customers on Private deployments might need manual backports, we'll list steps and include KMS/HSM checklists in the notes
09:30 Asha: anything else?
09:35 Marcus: one micro thing — can we add a perf regression alert for model compile time increases > 20%? I saw a spike in the nightly compile job
09:48 Priya: will add that to alerts
09:55 Asha: ok thanks everyone, I'll follow up with a summarized thread and update the roadmap board, if soak looks good we start the canary Dec 3rd
10:05 (end)
